  <bpmn:message id="Msg_PaymentReceived" name="Payment received"/>

  <bpmn:process id="Process_Insurer" name="Subrogation and recourse handling" isExecutable="false">

    <bpmn:task id="Task_CheckCase" name="Check case"/>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_RecourseSplit" name="Recourse really possible?"/>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="Task_SendPaymentRequest" name="Send request for payment to insurant" messageRef="Msg_PaymentRequest"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_CreateReminder" name="Create reminder"/>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Paid" name="Case closed (paid)"/>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_ReasoningSplit" name="Insurant right?"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_InsurantRight" name="Case closed (insurant right)"/>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="Task_ForwardToAgency" name="Forward case to collection agency" messageRef="Msg_CaseForwarded"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Forwarded" name="Case forwarded to collection agency"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_01" sourceRef="Start_Case" targetRef="Task_ObtainSubrogationInfo"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_02" sourceRef="Task_ObtainSubrogationInfo" targetRef="Gateway_SubrogationSplit"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_03" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_SubrogationSplit" targetRef="End_NoSubrogation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_04" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_SubrogationSplit" targetRef="Task_CheckCase"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_05" sourceRef="Task_CheckCase" targetRef="Gateway_RecourseSplit"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_06" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_RecourseSplit" targetRef="End_NoRecourse"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_07" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_RecourseSplit" targetRef="Task_SendPaymentRequest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_08" sourceRef="Task_SendPaymentRequest" targetRef="Task_CreateReminder"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_09" sourceRef="Task_CreateReminder" targetRef="Gateway_AwaitResponse"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="Gateway_AwaitResponse" targetRef="Event_PaymentReceived"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_11" sourceRef="Gateway_AwaitResponse" targetRef="Event_Disagreement"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_12" sourceRef="Gateway_AwaitResponse" targetRef="Event_DisagreementDeadline"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_13" sourceRef="Event_PaymentReceived" targetRef="Task_BookPayment"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_14" sourceRef="Task_BookPayment" targetRef="End_Paid"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_15" sourceRef="Event_Disagreement" targetRef="Task_CheckReasoning"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_16" sourceRef="Task_CheckReasoning" targetRef="Gateway_ReasoningSplit"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_17" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_ReasoningSplit" targetRef="End_InsurantRight"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_18" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_ReasoningSplit" targetRef="Gateway_ForwardMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_19" sourceRef="Event_DisagreementDeadline" targetRef="Gateway_ForwardMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_20" sourceRef="Gateway_ForwardMerge" targetRef="Task_ForwardToAgency"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_21" sourceRef="Task_ForwardToAgency" targetRef="End_Forwarded"/>
  </bpmn:process>

rules.instruction: When the description states that a branch or outcome ends with a closing or recording action performed by a participant, such as closing an item or making a booking, before the process outcome is reached: Model each such stated action as a task on that branch, placed after the decision or preceding step and before the end event of that outcome. Do not omit the action or connect the decision directly to the end event.
rules.situation: the description states that a branch or outcome ends with a closing or recording action performed by a participant, such as closing an item or making a booking, before the process outcome is reached

rules.instruction: When the description says the organization sends a request or case to an outside party and then waits for a reply from that party (such as a payment or an objection) that is received by the organization, without describing that party's own behaviour: Model the wait for the reply as an intermediate catch event in the organization's own process, placed after the request or case has been sent. Do not create a separate pool for the outside party, and do not add a message flow from the sending task to that party or from that party to the catch event.
rules.situation: the description says the organization sends a request or case to an outside party and then waits for a reply from that party (such as a payment or an objection) that is received by the organization, without describing that party's own behaviour

rules.instruction: When the description says a request is sent to a party and a follow-up is set in the meantime, and the process then waits for either a reply or a timed deadline, so the path depends on which occurs first: Model the wait as an event-based gateway. Give the awaited reply its own intermediate catch event, and give the timed follow-up its own intermediate timer catch event. Connect the timer catch event with a direct sequence flow to the activity the description says follows the missed deadline. Do not insert another gateway or an extra wait between the timer event and that activity, and do not route the timer branch into an unrelated activity or a new end event.
rules.situation: the description says a request is sent to a party and a follow-up is set in the meantime, and the process then waits for either a reply or a timed deadline, so the path depends on which occurs first

rules.instruction: When the description is written in the first person from the viewpoint of one acting role that performs the internal steps, and that role sends requests to, or receives replies and payments from, a separate external party which the description shows acting on its own (for example disagreeing or paying): Model the acting role as its own bpmn:participant pool that contains all of its internal steps, including the start and end events of its own work. Model the external party as a separate pool. Represent each request, payment and reply that crosses between the two as a message flow whose endpoints are in different pools. Do not place the acting role's steps in the external party's pool, and do not model the external party's actions as tasks of the acting role's pool.
rules.situation: the description is written in the first person from the viewpoint of one acting role that performs the internal steps, and that role sends requests to, or receives replies and payments from, a separate external party which the description shows acting on its own (for example disagreeing or paying)
